Answer: B
Reason: The frontal and lateral chest X-rays demonstrate a large anterior mediastinal mass that obscures the hilar vessels (positive hilum-overlay sign), confirming its anterior location. Additionally, there are bilateral basal opacities with meniscus signs consistent with pleural effusions, which, in the context of an aggressive anterior mediastinal mass, strongly suggests thymic carcinoma with pleural metastases.
